title: Objective
description: A funded, checkable question. The record's SHA-256 over its canonical serialization IS its id, so the verifier block is part of the objective's identity: editing an evaluator forks the objective rather than rescoring work already done against it.

goal.description: Identifier of the parent goal this objective decomposes.

statement.description: What is being asked, in prose, precisely enough that the verifier is recognisably a faithful encoding of it.

verifier.$comment: Per-kind fields are validated by the verifier itself, which returns INVALID_SPEC rather than a settling verdict when the spec is malformed.

reward.description: Integer units of account. Never a float -- floats do not round-trip identically across implementations.

ratchet.description: Progressive-bounty parameters. When present the objective pays along an improvement curve instead of once to a single winner. Part of the id, like the verifier.
ratchet.$comment: Field shape is validated by frontier::Ratchet, which reports a malformed block rather than settling on it.

confidentiality.description: When settled artifacts become public -- never whether. Omitted or null means 'public', and writing it explicitly produces byte-identical output, so this field did not reissue any pre-existing objective id. 'sealed' is declared so its cost is explicit but is refused at validation: paying for an artifact nobody may read requires a zero-knowledge proof that the pinned verifier accepts it, which is not implemented. Use 'embargoed' for delayed disclosure.
